manuscript.title: Evidence for variable life-cycle bottleneck positions under habitat fragmentation: a cross-system synthesis of plant interaction, mating and reproduction

established_before_this_paper: fragmentation often reduces pollination and reproductive success
pollination and reproductive responses can be positively associated across species/studies
pollen quantity and pollen quality/compatibility are biologically distinct
contribution: paired within-programme fragmentation response geometry with shared effect units and dependence
complete 12-programme paired process-function bottleneck census retaining resolved unresolved and not-testable programmes
evidence-gap audit showing quantity-level I measurements dominate and effective-mating I is absent
prospective bottleneck-localization design using Q-E-F rather than assuming one universally sensitive stage

current_claim_ceiling: the complete paired process-function census contains 12 independent programmes, 11 pair-testable, 4 resolved, 7 unresolved and 1 not-testable
the four resolved process-function mismatches include 3 downstream F-dominant and 1 upstream process-dominant programme
the two-direction resolved bottleneck pattern is not leave-one-programme-out robust because omitting ML001 Serapias removes the only upstream resolved direction
the five-cluster direct rejection is not Serapias-independent
the 8-programme I-F subset contains 3 resolved mismatches and all 3 are F-dominant
the 3/3 I-F directional pattern and 3:1 unified resolved split are descriptive and post hoc, not sign tests or prevalence estimates
all eight current I endpoints are quantity-level and none directly measures effective mating quality on the same I-F frame
the audited corpus provides evidence for more than one bottleneck position, while independent recurrence of the upstream direction remains unestablished
